title: Exact Adjoint Derivation for Product Residual
starting_point: V1691.2 derived branch/source adjoints. V1691.3 derives the bilinear product residual adjoint.
claim_boundary: Mathematical derivation only. No emitter, no simulation, no law validation.

objects.R_oplus_xy: product residual covector value for test pair (x,y)

product_residual.definition: δ_oplus[A](x,y) = T_A(x ⊕_p y) - (T_A x ⊕_q T_A y)
product_residual.component_space: V_oplus consists of bilinear residual maps over retained test pairs T_p.

variation.D1: left derivative of q-product with respect to first argument
variation.D2: right derivative of q-product with respect to second argument
variation.meaning: variation has one transported-product term and two output-product correction terms.

adjoint.pair_covector: C_xy = M_xy (x⊕_p y)^T - D1_q^*[M_xy] x^T - D2_q^*[M_xy] y^T
adjoint.first_order: If T_A≈I+A and L_A[Xi]≈Xi, then (D_Aδ_oplus)^*R = W_A^{-1} Σ_xy ω_xy C_xy

derivative_of_product.native_kernel_required: For any declared op_plus kernel, D1, D2, D1*, D2* must be derived from that kernel.

stationarity_contribution.meaning: product stress is a sum over retained test-pair covectors; it is not the scalar mean product defect.

why_v1690_failed: V1690 used scalar product defects and post-hoc component projection.
The exact product adjoint includes D1_q^* and D2_q^* correction terms.
Those terms couple transport variation to the native recombination product.
Without them, product compatibility cannot be separated from nulls component-wise.
forbidden: using mean product defect as Grad_oplus
choosing retained test pairs after seeing nulls
using E_source/E_stress to weight product pairs
replacing bilinear covector with scalar holonomy
